## The Story Today

The Strait of Hormuz has shifted from a point of contention to a primary diplomatic currency. The announcement of an agreement between Iran and Oman regarding traffic management ([The Jerusalem Post](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiakFVX3lxTE5RSXY3eXYwZ2cySXZ3UlE2YmlSbWFKeWlHejQ1SWNJNk5yNUxNRy05NlhGM2tQTjItdUNiZFAtc1d4WWR5TDlFdE9yZXY0VWNtS2txZ0xDOWtZRGtjaURtcEw2bzFIV0RoelE?oc=5), 2026-07-04) suggests Oman is successfully operationalizing its role as a back-channel mediator to stabilize maritime transit. This follows a broader regional push involving Qatar and Iraq to create a multilateral framework for the Strait ([Reuters](https://news.google.?oc=5), 2026-06-24).

However, this maritime stabilization is decoupled from the nuclear file, which remains in a state of public contradiction. While the IAEA chief previously indicated that inspections would proceed as part of a broader deal ([Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqwFBVV95cUxNVnZnbjBzNWg2N3R1eFNLelBNcDdsMkVaUGNpUUhKc2N2TWxtQTJkSnU4cXZ0aGtyN283SDVDNjNyQmpYNkxNUW9fVDFOcXRUOHRmYy1LVzZtbjRiMlprYWVvYk5iVDR1VDRRaVZDdFdHX1E2ZkhCcFBHa3FiRWJuVFhObDU4dkttTHdKX3NMMEc4bGxtS3NsODRzRk4zbzF2S25ORkgyR1Y2Sm8?oc=5), 2026-06-24), he has explicitly confirmed that inspectors have not yet returned to the ground ([WANA News Agency](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifEFVX3lxTFA5cTRCZkM0SlpkeFpfcURKM2NMVkQtMDZRdHVyd0ZiU3RNbnVlaHZnNVdjdkFtVENraUdaa3lDamdFeEpHNzdQbGQwaTBQaG5aenNJSnNzc3FVMVBLakY2bEpjQnhiVWlGNVl4TVVvY2JaSG81dk5RUlNNbUU?oc=5), 2026-07-03). A strategic tension is emerging between the UN Security Council and regional mediators. While Oman and Qatar are securing tactical wins on navigation and hotlines ([arabnews.jp](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiZEFVX3lxTE9JajlUb3djMl9INDh3c1NuRWRCX01Qa3FfTi1Fa3NEenlVWXBwbnJ5NFRBNEdTd19kQXhRS2ZXM3JUZ0hzTU5LUTdaUGplZ3ZnQW40SkVoQ0FYNE1ONzVvSkZoNFA?oc=5), 2026-06-24), the rejection of a UNSC draft resolution regarding the Strait ([News On AIR](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxQX2pUcWFsV0kzQk1OeTQtTVVVNnE2b0C3ZTI0NXc4WklfTi1rdnlDSDhoUkQyWTBfSFY4YXVuNTF5OFA4WFF0c2xOQzF6cWJjbzM0RlJfdGNBTTFHX3F1a3pEQmRMMjlmZ0dEeTV1dmJjZHdfay1nVGpzeGp6Zy1DX0RneEIxS3Vya25XNDVON2JabE4zaTNxR0xLV0RCTmRjZ0ljZnphQlhmV2pNcDdJV3o4LXMwVEJmT1dnNVF2cXM?oc=5), 2026-07-05) indicates that multilateral formalization is lagging behind bilateral pragmatism.
